head: SatData: offline compass and GPS app for iPhone that works without signal
dek: SatData is a 4.99-dollar iPhone app from developer Matthew Avery that shows your position, altitude, heading and sun and moon times with no mobile signal, explained in plain words. It was #37 in Navigation on the US App Store's paid chart on 23 November.
details: It also shows speed and air pressure, gives each reading a quality rating from Excellent to Poor, and its compass shows true and magnetic north. A sky section lists sunrise, sunset, golden hour and the moon's phase. You can mark up to 20 waypoints and follow an arrow, with distance and bearing, back to a car, tent or trailhead in a straight line. A survey mode averages GPS readings for 30 seconds to 2 minutes, and data can be exported as GPX, CSV, JSON, NMEA or text. It's a one-time purchase with no subscription, in-app purchases or ads, and the listing says it collects no data; only Apple's map tiles need a connection. The developer says it's a reference tool, not a safety or certified navigation device.
where: iPhone (iOS 18 or later), also Mac with Apple silicon and Vision Pro; out since 10 October 2026
means: If you hike, camp or go geocaching where there's no coverage, this app gives you a compass, altitude and a way back to a saved spot without a connection.
todo: Check the App Store listing; save a waypoint before you set off, and carry a map too, since the developer says readings can be wrong.
thumb_words: OFFLINE COMPASS APP: NO SIGNAL NEEDED
